summary: Any array value can change the total remainder, so one complete input scan matches the problem's linear inspection lower bound.

optimality.argument: For any position an adversary can alter that positive input value by one while keeping every inspected value fixed, changing the total modulo any k greater than one and potentially changing the answer. A correct worst-case algorithm must inspect all n values. Summing once and taking one remainder performs O(1) work per value and meets this Omega(n) lower bound.

replacement_checks.evidence: An uninspected array entry can be changed by one and thereby change the required remainder and operation count.
The accepted implementation visits each value once to compute the sum, then performs one modulo operation.
Authored fixtures cover k equal to one, the maximum k, a single element, zero remainder, remainder k minus one, maximum values, and sums below k.
